## Summary
Faster MiniMax-M3 sparse attention on Hopper: Triton decode and prefill kernels with tiled block pointers (Triton >= 3.9), fp16-widened decode for fp8 KV on the paged path, and a fused bf16-to-fp8 cast in the fused K/V/index store.

## Changes to existing code
- On Hopper with `fp8_e4m3` KV, the sparse index K cache is stored in fp8 (it was bf16 unless fp8 attention GEMMs were on). Other platforms keep the previous dtype.
- The fused K/V/index store also handles an unscaled bf16-to-fp8_e4m3 cast (CUDA only); other inputs use the separate stores as before.

## Verification
- Kernel tests on H200: `test_minimax_sparse_fp8_attn_gemm.py` 88 passed; the fused store cast is bit-exact against `x.float().clamp(-448, 448).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)`.
- MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on 8xH200, H200 cookbook recipe plus `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, sgl-eval 0.1.3, this PR vs. fp16 widening disabled:

| | GSM8K (greedy, 2 runs) | AIME26 (avg@8) |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | 96.21 / 96.06 | 91.25 |
| widening off | 96.36 / 96.51 | 93.75 |

The between-arm per-question divergence and correctness flips are within the run-to-run noise of either arm.

Cut from #45925 (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash support) at 10e655aa98.

+"""Masked tile addressing for the MiniMax sparse attention kernels.
+
+Triton >= 3.9 removed ``tl.make_block_ptr``. These helpers return the
+``(pointers, mask)`` pair that a block pointer with ``boundary_check`` on every
+dimension described, so
+
+    tl.load(make_block_ptr(...), boundary_check=..., padding_option="zero")
+    tl.store(make_block_ptr(...), x, boundary_check=...)
+
+become
+
+    ptrs, mask = tile_ptrs_2d(...)
+    tl.load(ptrs, mask=mask, other=0.0)
+    tl.store(ptrs, x, mask=mask)
+
+Offsets are widened to int64 like block-pointer offsets, so large strides do not
+overflow. ``tl.advance`` becomes an explicit offset update at the call site; the
+shape bounds stay absolute, exactly as block pointers checked them.
+"""
+
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def tile_ptrs_1d(base, n, stride, off, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    idx = off + tl.arange(0, BLOCK).to(tl.int64)
+    return base + idx * stride, idx < n
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def tile_ptrs_2d(
+    base,
+    n_rows,
+    n_cols,
+    stride_r,
+    stride_c,
+    row_off,
+    col_off,
+    BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_C: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    rows = row_off + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R).to(tl.int64)
+    cols = col_off + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_C).to(tl.int64)
+    ptrs = base + rows[:, None] * stride_r + cols[None, :] * stride_c
+    mask = (
+        (rows[:, None] >= 0)
+        & (rows[:, None] < n_rows)
+        & (cols[None, :] >= 0)
+        & (cols[None, :] < n_cols)
+    )
+    return ptrs, mask
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def tile_ptrs_3d(
+    base,
+    n0,
+    n1,
+    n2,
+    stride0,
+    stride1,
+    stride2,
+    off0,
+    BLOCK0: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK1: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK2: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    i0 = off0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK0).to(tl.int64)
+    i1 = tl.arange(0, BLOCK1).to(tl.int64)
+    i2 = tl.arange(0, BLOCK2).to(tl.int64)
+    ptrs = (
+        base
+        + i0[:, None, None] * stride0
+        + i1[None, :, None] * stride1
+        + i2[None, None, :] * stride2
+    )
+    mask = (
+        (i0[:, None, None] < n0) & (i1[None, :, None] < n1) & (i2[None, None, :] < n2)
+    )
+    return ptrs, mask
